raw_prompt: Build an authentication platform with token revocation.

cumulative_requirements.title: Authentication Platform Core
cumulative_requirements.description: The system must provide authentication capabilities to verify user identities.
cumulative_requirements.justification: Directly stated in the prompt 'Build an authentication platform'.

cumulative_requirements.title: Token Revocation Mechanism
cumulative_requirements.description: The system must support the ability to revoke issued authentication tokens.
cumulative_requirements.justification: Directly stated in the prompt 'with token revocation'.

cumulative_requirements.title: Token Blacklist or Validation State Store
cumulative_requirements.description: The system must maintain a state store (such as a revocation list or blacklist) to verify if an incoming token has been explicitly invalidated prior to its natural expiration.
cumulative_requirements.justification: Why 1: Stateless tokens (e.g., JWTs) remain valid until expiration by design, creating a security risk upon logout or compromise. Why 2: A stateful lookup mechanism (e.g., revocation cache, token ID blacklist, or incremented token versioning) must intercept validation flows to check revocation status. Why 3: No token marked as revoked can ever be successfully accepted for authenticated operations.

cumulative_requirements.title: Token Format and Cryptographic Standard
cumulative_requirements.description: The specific token format (e.g., JWT, PASETO) and signing algorithm (e.g., Ed25519, RS256, HS256) are unstated.
cumulative_requirements.justification: The prompt does not specify the token standard, cryptographic algorithms, or transport protocols.

cumulative_requirements.title: Storage Backend and Persistence Provider
cumulative_requirements.description: The underlying database or persistence engine for user credentials and revocation state is unstated.
cumulative_requirements.justification: The prompt does not specify database engines (e.g., PostgreSQL, Redis, DynamoDB) for storing state.

cumulative_requirements.title: Token Revocation Propagation and Latency Boundary
cumulative_requirements.description: The system must define and enforce a strict upper bound on propagation latency for token revocation across all validation nodes to ensure revoked tokens are rejected immediately.
cumulative_requirements.justification: 1. When a token is revoked, distributed validation nodes evaluating incoming requests may cache validation results or lack synchronous updates; 2. Without a guaranteed synchronization bound or immediate check against a central revocation store, a compromised or logged-out token remains usable until cache expiration; 3. Therefore, a strict latency boundary or bypass check must be enforced to preserve the security guarantee of the revocation mechanism.

cumulative_requirements.title: Revocation State Store Failure Mode and Fail-Closed Guard
cumulative_requirements.description: The system must enforce a fail-closed policy if the token revocation state store becomes unavailable or experiences a timeout during token validation.
cumulative_requirements.justification: 1. State stores used for blacklisting or revocation checks can suffer network partitions, crashes, or timeouts; 2. If the system defaults to failing open (allowing tokens when the blacklist cannot be reached), an attacker could disrupt the state store to bypass revocation checks entirely; 3. Therefore, an explicit fail-closed guard is required to deny authentication when revocation state integrity cannot be verified.

cumulative_requirements.title: Revocation Store Storage Exhaustion and Pruning Policy
cumulative_requirements.description: The system must implement a retention and pruning policy for the token revocation state store to prevent unbounded growth and storage exhaustion.
cumulative_requirements.justification: 1. Every token revocation adds an entry to the state store that must typically persist at least until the token's natural expiration timestamp; 2. Storing expired token identifiers indefinitely leads to uncontrolled database size inflation and degradation of lookup performance; 3. Therefore, an automated pruning policy tied to token expiration timestamps is mandatory to ensure long-term data integrity and system stability.

cumulative_requirements.title: Unstated Identity Provider Integration Boundary
cumulative_requirements.description: The external upstream identity providers, enterprise directories (e.g., LDAP, Active Directory), or federation protocols (e.g., OIDC, SAML 2.0) are unstated.
cumulative_requirements.justification: No mention of upstream identity federation or source-of-truth directories exists in the baseline specification.

cumulative_requirements.title: Network Transport and API Protocol Unstated
cumulative_requirements.description: The specific network protocols and transport mechanisms (e.g., gRPC, HTTPS/REST, WebSockets) utilized for authentication requests and revocation checks are unstated.
cumulative_requirements.justification: The specification lacks any reference to the communication protocol or interface layer specifications.

cumulative_requirements.title: Crash Recovery and Power Loss Invariant for Revocation State
cumulative_requirements.description: The system must guarantee that durable revocation state records are successfully synchronized or flushed to non-volatile storage prior to acknowledging token issuance or revocation confirmation, preventing post-crash revocation state amnesia.
cumulative_requirements.justification: Without durability guarantees upon unexpected power loss or abrupt node termination, revoked tokens could become un-revoked after a system restart, compromising security.

cumulative_requirements.title: Graceful Shutdown and Drain Operational Boundary
cumulative_requirements.description: During a graceful shutdown or deployment lifecycle event, the authentication platform must drain in-flight validation requests and complete pending token revocation propagations before terminating worker processes.
cumulative_requirements.justification: To prevent request dropping or incomplete synchronization of revocation states during rolling deployments or scaling events, a graceful drain protocol is required.
